stories.headline: New benchmark evaluates AI agents on open scientific questions from US labs
stories.summary: Carnegie Mellon University and US Department of Energy labs released the "Into the Unknown" benchmark to test whether AI agents can independently conduct follow-up research on open scientific problems. In the first round, none of the 135 submissions from nine agents satisfied all expert criteria, with many failing integrity checks.
stories.whyItMatters: It shows current AI agents still struggle with autonomous scientific research, highlighting gaps before they can be trusted for real-world discovery.

stories.headline: Video Rebirth releases HyperFlow H3 Flash, a 13.7B parameter video and audio generation model
stories.summary: HyperFlow H3 Flash compresses the MiniMax-H3 model to 13.7 billion parameters and can run in as few as six steps. The model fits on consumer GPUs with 24 GB of memory and generates synchronized video and stereo audio.
stories.whyItMatters: It makes high-quality video-audio generation accessible to a wider range of developers and creators.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches Cyber Mission to help secure critical infrastructure and open-source software
stories.summary: Anthropic announced a long-term Cyber Mission that includes a program for defending critical infrastructure and a free security scanning tool for open-source projects. The effort aims to improve the security of essential systems and software.
stories.whyItMatters: It provides resources and tools to strengthen the security of vital digital infrastructure.

stories.headline: Anthropic updates its Usage Policy effective November 12
stories.summary: Anthropic released a revised Usage Policy that clarifies rules for new model capabilities and consolidates restrictions on deceptive campaigns and artificial activity. The changes take effect on November 12.
stories.whyItMatters: Clearer policy helps users understand permissible uses and reduces misuse of Anthropic models.

stories.headline: Anthropic commits $150 million to the U.S. Genesis Mission for scientific research
stories.summary: Anthropic will invest $150 million over three years to support the federal Genesis Mission, providing Claude and related tools to more than 15 U.S. government agencies, including NASA and NIH. The funding aims to accelerate scientific discovery across multiple domains.
stories.whyItMatters: The investment expands access to advanced AI tools for government research, potentially speeding up breakthroughs in science and health.
